text.p: On overnight commodity markets, copper prices rose above US$1,950 on the London Metal Exchange on short term technical tightness. Aluminium recovered in sympathy.
Gold prices rose as funds taking profits in equity and bond markets moved into gold.
Wheat prices closed lower on thin volumes as traders repositioned ahead of the USDA crop report on Friday.
Oil prices fell away with U.S. heating oil prices, which are correcting from strong rallies recently.
Sugar prices ended up a touch.

Copper prices pushed above $1,950 during Thursday afternoon LME trading, with the firmer trend assisting the aluminium market in recovering from early fresh 2-1/2 year lows. Traders said short-term technical tightness on the LME helped copper break back above $1,950, with November and December dates in keen demand. The tightness reflects a finely balanced short-term supply/demand picture, with LME warehouse inventories expected to fall again on Friday. If the current upturn is maintained the next objective is the crucial $1,970 level. Last trade on the kerb was at $1,958 a tonne, up $30 from Wednesday's kerb. Copper's rally, as well as short-term oversold warnings, helped aluminium recover from midmorning blues when prices slumped to new 2-1/2 year lows of $1,305 when investment banks and speculators lined up to sell. The expected short-covering helped prices recover and move back up to $1,332 a tonne, a $9 gain on the day, although a test of $1,300 is expected in the not-too-distant future. IPAI producer stocks rose marginally in August, but more pertinently LME warehouse stocks are likely to register an increase on Friday. Nickel prices managed to recover from under $7,100 - a level seen as short-term technical support - with the market pushing above $7,200 to settle at $7,220, up $90 from Wednesday. The zinc market recovered from its midsession wobble down to near $1,030, helped by copper, and prices edged back up to close the session at $1,033, down just $2 with the market comfortable in a $1,030/40 jobbing range.

CBOT wheat futures closed lower amid thin volume with positioning featured before the release at 0730 CDT Friday of USDA's October crop production and supply/demand reports, traders said. Pressure also came from a lower-than-expected number in Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report, they said. USDA early Thursday said U.S. wheat net export sales for the week ended October 3 were at 296,200 tonnes, 50 percent below the previous week and 40 percent below the four-week average. Wheat closed three cents per bushel lower to two higher, with December down three at $4.24 a bushel.

NYMEX heating oil prices plunged Thursday after a sell-off in gas oil futures in London accelerated profit-taking started Wednesday, with crude and gasoline retracing gains made on heat's recent torrid rise. "It was a correction that was overdue. There was a lot of length getting out," said a trader. November heating oil settled off 3.05 cents at 70.92 cents a gallon. November gas oil on London's IPE settled $13.75 lower at 225.00 a tonne. Profit-taking started Wednesday after the American Petroleum Institute reported a larger-than-expected build in distillate inventories. Traders said the correction was mostly over since heating oil's losses in the past two days have created a 50 percent correction from the latest short-term uptrend which started with a breakout mid-September. November crude settled 81 cents lower at $24.26 a barrel and November gasoline ended 2.07 cents lower at 63.52 cents a gallon. Crude got some support on news OPEC is likely to hold its oil output quota at 25.03 million bpd, but the news was not bullish enough to buffer heat's downdraft, traders said.

New York precious metals futures recovered further Thursday, reaching two-week highs as chart resistance levels were breached, trade demand improved, and investors taking profits in equities and bond markets were tempted back into commodities, analysts said. "COMEX warehouse stocks of gold and silver have been falling, suggesting demand is up, while U.S. equity and bond markets have come off their highs in the past week, leading investors back into precious metals and prompting more fund shortcovering," FIMAT USA floor trader John Tyree said. COMEX December gold ended up $1.00 at $384.50 an ounce, after seeing an intraday high at $385.30, the highest level since Sept 26.In
New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted at $382.00/50 versus the London afternoon fix of $381.75 and Wednesday's New York close at $381.00/50.

Shortcovering by funds lifted CSCE world sugar futures from below unchanged to close just under session peaks, possibly setting the stage for higher prices Friday, dealers said. Most-active March contract climbed from a low of 10.69 cents a lb, where sell stops have been cited, to settle near the day's high of 10.89 cents. In fundamental news, Romania said 1996 sugar output, expected to exceed 280,000 tonnes, will fall short of demand, raising the likelihood for raw sugar imports. A floor source cited talk that Russia bought more than 100,000 tonnes of sugar, but market sources were unable to verify the rumor.
